meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'trouble, misfortune' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'trouble, misfortune' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну, допустим, я жулик. А ты жадина и не помогаешь людям в беде.
examples.trans: All right, let's say I'm a crook. But you're greedy, and you don't help people in trouble.

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: steadfast in allegiance or affection

examples.text: Ты мой главный учитель и верный наставник.
examples.trans: You are my main teacher and true mentor.

examples.text: А я вообще очень верная женщина.
examples.trans: And I am actually a very loyal woman.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
short forms виноват / виновата / виноваты are used for 'it's my/your fault'

examples.text: Я ни в чём не виноват.
examples.trans: I'm not to blame for anything.

meanings.note: Ordinal number. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('second').

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').
Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
Дай! = give (me)!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: играть в + accusative (a game/sport)

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: comparative крепче = tighter, more firmly
Крепко спать = sleep soundly. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Смотри, держи меня за ногу. Вот так! Крепче держи!
examples.trans: Look, hold me by the leg. Like that! Hold tighter!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
From Latin 'momentum' (movement, brief span of time).

examples.text: А мне что-то уже не хочется. Момент упущен.
examples.trans: Somehow I don't feel like it anymore. The moment has passed.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Art or sound of music. Common feminine noun meaning 'music' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We'll find some music right now.
I like listening to quiet music.

examples.text: Вань, посмотри! — Смотри, работает! Сейчас музыку найдём.
examples.trans: Vanya, look! — Look, it works! We'll find some music right now.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Experienced and trusted adviser. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ставник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'mentor, tutor' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The teacher became my main mentor.

examples.text: Ты мой главный учитель и верный наставник.
examples.trans: You are my main teacher and true mentor.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
in an awkward or embarrassed manner

examples.text: Да, под такую музыку обниматься немного неловко.
examples.trans: Yes, it is a bit awkward hugging to such music.
It turned out somewhat awkward, Kostya.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

обниматься.gloss: to hug each other, to embrace

meanings.en: to hug, to embrace each other
meanings.note: Reciprocal reflexive verb. Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ниматься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hug each other, to embrace', paired with 'обняться'.

examples.text: Что вы обнимаетесь? Вы с ума сошли!
examples.trans: Why are you two hugging? Have you lost your minds!

examples.text: Да, под такую музыку обниматься немного неловко.
examples.trans: Yes, it is a bit awkward hugging to such music.

meanings.en: to hug, to put one's arms around
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hug, to embrace', paired with 'обнимать'.

examples.text: Юля, ну иди сюда, не обижайся! Иди обниму!
examples.trans: Yulia, come here, don't be upset! Come let me hug you!
The father hugged his daughter tightly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: commissioned member of armed or security forces

examples.trans: He is an experienced army officer.

examples.text: Я очень плохой офицер и плохой руководитель.
examples.trans: I am a very bad officer and a bad leader.

examples.text: Толя, ты прекрасный руководитель и отличный офицер!
examples.trans: Tolya, you are a wonderful leader and an excellent officer!

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cry, to weep', paired with 'заплакать'.

examples.trans: Why is the little girl crying?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: + instrumental (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'under' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'under' in everyday speech.
Под мою ответственность. Core Russian prep meaning 'under' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The cat is under the table.

examples.text: Хорошо, давайте три. Под мою личную ответственность.
examples.trans: All right, let's say three. On my personal responsibility.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go, to set off (by car, bus, train)
meanings.note: Мы поедем = We'll be off. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle), to set off', paired with 'ехать'.

examples.trans: All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: On foot. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, wonderful').

examples.text: Посмотри, какой у нас город прекрасный. Озёра, луга.
examples.trans: Look what a beautiful town we have. Lakes, meadows.

meanings.note: military reconnaissance or intelligence gathering

examples.text: Я бы с тобой в разведку пошёл.
examples.trans: I would go into reconnaissance with you.

examples.text: Я бы с тобой в разведку пошёл!
examples.trans: I would go into reconnaissance with you!

meanings.note: Cause ruin to a family or thing. Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'рушить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to destroy, to ruin', paired with 'разрушать'.

examples.text: Ты разрушил мою семью своими фотографиями!
examples.trans: You destroyed my family with your photos!

examples.text: Ты разрушил такой прекрасный и сентиментальный момент!
examples.trans: You ruined such a wonderful and sentimental moment!

meanings.note: To affect with tender feelings. Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'трогать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to move, to touch emotionally', paired with 'растрогивать'.

examples.text: Соколов, ты меня сейчас очень сильно растрогал.
examples.trans: Sokolov, you have moved me very deeply right now.

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'head, leader, manager' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She is the new head of the headquarters.

examples.text: Я новый руководитель предвыборного штаба Павла Юрьевича.
examples.trans: I am the new head of Pavel Yuryevich's campaign headquarters.

examples.text: Здравствуйте! Я не журналистка. Я руководитель штаба Ивана Самсонова.
examples.trans: Hello! I'm not a journalist. I'm the head of Ivan Samsonov's campaign.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ентиментальный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sentimental, soft').

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: Informal. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sit, to be sitting', paired with 'посидеть'.

examples.trans: Why are you sitting in the corner?

meanings.note: Adverb of degree. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

спешить.gloss: to hurry, be in a rush

meanings.en: to hurry, rush, be in a hurry
meanings.note: куда ты спешишь? = where are you rushing to?

examples.trans: What happened? Where are you rushing to?
We are in a big hurry for the train.
Wait a bit, Sokolov. Do not hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').
'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Core Russian pron meaning 'such, like this' in everyday speech.
softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: a regional office of a government service

Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'правление'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'department, directorate; control' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He works at the main directorate.

meanings.note: irregular nominative plural учителя

examples.text: Славик, ты слышишь, что учителя говорят?
examples.trans: Slavik, do you hear what the teachers are saying?

examples.text: Наш учитель истории очень интересно рассказывает.
examples.trans: Our history teacher tells stories very interestingly.

examples.text: Ты мой главный учитель и верный наставник.
examples.trans: You are my main teacher and true mentor.

meanings.note: How something is done. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
As an answer. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
